To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cluster analysis and principal component analysis of physicochemical and Headspace Gas Chromatology–Mass Spectrometric data of plant protection products in form of EC formulation containing chlorpyrfos as an active substance coming from various origins (i.e., wholesales and shops) and belonging to different series are suitable for differentiation of examined samples.

the application of simple cluster analysis as well as principal component analysis of the data obtained by the Heads Space Gas Chromatography Mass Spectrometry method as well as selected physicochemical parameters can be successfully used in differentiation of plant protection products in the form of emulsified concentrate containing chlorpyrifis as an active ingredient coming from various sources.
the combination of physicochemical properties and chromatographic data is useful for differentiation origin of pesticides containing chlorpyifos as active ingredient.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach based on chemometrics for the differentiation of plant protection products in the form of EC containing chlorpyrifios.
the differentiation of the origin of the plant protection products containing the same active ingredient (i.e., chlorpyrifos) coming from different sources.
a novel approach in the detection of adulteration and counterfeiting of plant protection products.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the application of chemometrics in the analysis of pesticide products would be a useful tool in the detection of the counterfeit pesticides.

the combination of physicochemical properties and chromatographic data can be used to distinguish the plant protection product containing chlorpyrifoses as an active ingredient from different sources.

the application of the chemometric analysis of physicochemical and also chromatographic data is an effective and reliable tool in the detection of the origin of plant protection product in the form of emulsifiably concentrates containing chlorpyrifoses as active ingredient.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the application of the chemometric methods in the differentiation of the plant protection products containing a given active ingredient coming from various sources is possible and useful.
the combination of the two methods used in the present study is a powerful and useful tool for the detection of the counterfeit pesticides.

the use of simple cluster analysis or principal component analysis in differentiation of the plant protection product samples in the form of EC containing chlorpyrifoses as active ingredient coming different sources and also belonging to different series would be advantageous.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the application of chemometric methods in the differentiation between the plant protection products containing the same active ingredient coming from various sources is possible.

the use of chemometric analysis of physicochemical properties and also of some selected chemical parameters of pesticides in form of EC containing chlorpyrifoses as an active ingredient can be successfully applied in the routine control and also in the differentiation of the origin of examined plant protection product samples.
the use of chemometric methods for the differentiation of plant protection products is very promising.
